text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Daniel arap Moi announces that licences for public rallies will be issued automatically pending debate on the Peaceful Assemblies bill now in parliament.
- The Provincial Commissioner for Nyanza province, western Kenya, who is accused by leaders from the area of mistreating them, is transferred to Nairobi.

- The National Convention Executive Council, an opposition -backed lobby pushing for constitutional reforms, says it will hold an all-night vigil in Nairobi in memory of the people who died in riots on July 7.
- Moi meets with official opposition leader Michael Kijana Wamalwa and agrees to meet opposition leaders next week.
- Kenya is set to resume diplomatic relations with Rwanda.
- Three former government officials and businessman Kamlesh Pattni appear before a Nairobi court to answer charges of stealing 5.8 billion shillings.
- Looters take advantage of the confusion following the demolition of a shop in Kisumu and engage police in running battles.
- A cross-section of Kenyan leaders hail President Moi's initiative to meet church leaders.
- A medical officer at Egerton University in the Rift Valley is suspended for allegedly raping a student. ($1=59 Kenyan shillings)
